$comment: Guidance for matching model capability to work type. This is advisory, not enforced by any script — the operator selects the model. Recorded here so routing decisions are explicit and reviewable rather than habitual.

useFor: scientific modelling and numerical scheme selection
debugging where the mechanism is unknown
deep.rationale: Work where being wrong is expensive and the error would not be obvious.

useFor: implementing a specified unit against a clear contract
writing tests from stated acceptance criteria
mechanical refactoring with a safety net
standard.rationale: Well-specified work where the contract carries most of the difficulty.

useFor: worker agents in a fan-out with a strong output contract
fast.rationale: Narrow, verifiable tasks where the output is easy to check.

escalationRules.when: the same task has failed twice at the current tier
escalationRules.action: escalate one tier rather than retrying a third time
escalationRules.rationale: Two failures usually indicate the task exceeds the tier, not bad luck. A third retry costs more than the escalation.

escalationRules.when: the task is irreversible or outward-facing
escalationRules.action: use the deep tier regardless of apparent simplicity

escalationRules.when: the output cannot be cheaply verified
escalationRules.rationale: Cheap generation plus expensive verification is a false economy.

escalationRules.when: verification is a mechanical check the harness can run
escalationRules.action: a lower tier is acceptable — let the gate catch the error
escalationRules.rationale: A structure check or a failing test is a cheaper reviewer than a stronger model.

antiPatterns: Routing by task length rather than by task difficulty.
Using the deep tier for work whose output a script already validates.
Retrying a failed task at the same tier more than twice.
Fanning out to many parallel agents when one agent's context would hold the whole task.
Choosing a tier by habit and never recording the choice.
notes: Model identifiers here are the ones documented for this environment as of 2026-07-28. Verify against current documentation before depending on an exact string.
No routing is enforced automatically. Record the model actually used in the session log — that field is what makes routing decisions reviewable after the fact.
